scripts.title: Scripts
scripts.hint: Recipes of structured steps that run against one or several SSH connections. Passwords are never stored: steps only reference the keyring or KeePass.
scripts.empty: No scripts yet. Create one with “New script”.
scripts.delete_confirm: Delete “{name}”? This action cannot be undone.
scripts.import_invalid: The file does not look like a valid script runbook.
scripts.import_ignored: {count} line(s) in the file were not recognized and will not be imported. The script will be incomplete.

err.not_object: The script is not an object.
err.profile_needs_id: The connection target needs a connection.
err.folder_needs_recursive: The folder needs the recursive flag.
err.adhoc_needs_profile: The selection needs at least one connection.
err.step_not_object: the step is not an object.
err.waitregex_needs_pattern: the 'wait for pattern' step needs a pattern.
err.waitregex_invalid_pattern: the 'wait for pattern' step has an invalid pattern.

scripts.preview_empty: The script has no command steps to send.
scripts.no_targets: The target does not resolve to any connection.
scripts.abort_close_msg: The script is still running. Abort it and close?
scripts.log_draining: Waiting for the last command to finish…
scripts.history_hint: The latest runs saved on this machine. Reopen them to see their log and output, or export them to a file.
scripts.bg_running: A script is already running; showing its progress
scripts.cred_keepass_locked: The KeePass database is locked; unlock it to pick an entry.
scripts.cred_missing: Complete the run credentials: the password or the selection is missing.
scripts.rec_need_ssh: Open and connect an SSH session to record a script from it.
scripts.rec_started: Recording. Type in the terminal; when done, press “Stop and edit”.
scripts.rec_stopped: Recorded {n} steps. Review them before saving.
scripts.rec_truncated: Recording stopped at the step limit ({n}).

prefs_commands.title: Snippets and commands
prefs_commands.hint: Snippets are inserted into the active terminal; local commands run on this machine. Both accept variables like ${host}, ${user}, ${var:name} and ${ask:Label}, and are quick to find from the command palette.
prefs_commands.toast_no_session: Open a terminal session to insert the snippet.
prefs_commands.toast_timeout: {name} exceeded the {secs}s limit and was stopped
prefs_commands.timeout_hint: A local command that never finishes is stopped when the time limit runs out, along with any processes it started. You can always cancel it by hand from the notice while it runs.
prefs_commands.output_hint: How much output is kept from each command. Anything beyond it is discarded and the notice says so; the command itself keeps running normally.

modal_localcmd.name: Name
modal_localcmd.command_hint: Runs on this machine with the system shell.
modal_localcmd.hint_shell: Runs on this machine with the system shell. Accepts ${host}, ${user}, ${var:name} and ${ask:Label}.
modal_localcmd.hint_url: Opens in the browser. Accepts ${var:name} and ${ask:Label}.
modal_localcmd.hint_path: Opens with the system's default application.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics report
diagnostics.hint: Builds a report with the version, platform, your preferences and the latest events, to attach to a bug report. It never includes passwords, passphrases, tokens or terminal contents; hosts and paths are anonymised unless you allow them here.
diagnostics.include_hosts_hint: Without this option each host appears as a stable alias (“host-3f2a”): lines can still be correlated without revealing where you connect.
diagnostics.include_paths_hint: Without this option only the shape of each path is reported (depth and extension), never its contents.

layout.restore_offer: {n} tab(s) from your last session ready to restore

firstrun.title: Get to work
firstrun.hint: Quick connect saves a profile with that target and opens the session; the password is asked on connect and goes only to the keyring.

trash.title: Trash
trash.empty_confirm: Empty the trash? Items will be permanently lost.
trash.restored_password_hint: Passwords never go through the trash: you will be asked again when connecting.

blocks.none: No command blocks in this session. The shell must emit OSC 133 (bash/zsh/fish with prompt integration).
blocks.fallback_hint: Blocks inferred with the prompt regex: the shell does not emit OSC 133.
blocks.panel_empty: No blocks detected in this session.
blocks.goto_title: Jump to the block in the terminal
blocks.diff_no_neighbour: There is no other block to compare with.
blocks.diff_truncated: The changed section was too large to align line by line: it is shown as a full replacement.

palette.title: Command palette
palette.action_diff_block: Compare block with the previous one

health.title: Health check
health.hint: DNS resolution and TCP connection with a time limit only; it never attempts to log in.
health.no_targets: No connections with a host to check.

activity.session_stale: Session "{name}" is not responding after the suspend; it may be dead.

sidebar.workspace_confirm_delete_full: This workspace contains connections. They will be deleted with it. Continue?
sidebar.favorites_empty: You haven't favorited any connection yet.
sidebar.empty_hint: Create your first SSH, RDP, SFTP or FTP profile to get started.
sidebar.favorites_empty_hint: Mark a connection as favorite from its context menu and it'll show up here.

close_local_shell.title: Close local console
close_local_shell.message: The local console is running a process. Close anyway?

view_layout.broadcast: Replicate input to all panes (Broadcast Input)
view_layout.resizer_reset_hint: Drag to resize · double-click to even out

external.session_open: {proto} session open in an external window

promote_master.message: Turn this profile's own password into a reusable master credential.
promote_master.no_password: The profile has no saved password to promote.
promote_master.invalid_name: Invalid name: no spaces; starts with a letter or “_” and only letters, digits, “_”, “-” or “.”.
promote_master.duplicate_name: A master credential with that name already exists.
promote_master.delete_own_message: Delete the profile's own password from the keyring? The profile will use the master credential.
promote_master.done: Master credential “{name}” created and assigned to the profile.

shell_child.open_failed: Could not open the new shell
shell_child.close_children_warning: Tabs opened on this connection will close too.

tab_rename.label: Alias

modal_conn.name: Name
modal_conn.rdp_display_hint: Resizable window and full screen need Windows 8 / Server 2012 or newer.
modal_conn.notes_hint: Local text for profile reminders. Avoid storing secrets here.
modal_conn.master_cred_missing: The referenced credential no longer exists. Pick another.
modal_conn.master_cred_none: No master credentials. Create them in Preferences.
modal_conn.master_cred_hint: The password will be taken from the selected master credential when connecting.
modal_conn.keepass_locked: The KeePass database is locked. Unlock it in Preferences.
modal_conn.keepass_entry_status_not_found: The selected entry does not exist in the unlocked database.
modal_conn.keepass_search_ph: Search by title, username, URL or group…
modal_conn.keepass_property_hint: Defaults to the password. Change this field to reference any property of the KeePass entry.
modal_conn.save_password: Remember password in the system keyring
modal_conn.save_passphrase: Save passphrase in the system keyring
modal_conn.extra_users_hint: Alternative identities, each with its own authentication (password, SSH key or master credential). Connecting uses the primary one; right-click to pick “Connect as another user”.
modal_conn.follow_cwd: Track terminal CWD in the SFTP panel
modal_conn.follow_cwd_hint: When CWD is enabled in the SFTP panel, inject a shell hook (bash/zsh) that reports the current directory. Turn it off if you don't want PROMPT_COMMAND modified.
modal_conn.keep_alive_hint: 0 = disabled. Sends a keepalive packet to the server every N seconds to prevent NAT timeouts.
modal_conn.cmd_notify_secs_hint: This profile's own threshold for the long-command-finished notice. Empty = use the global threshold from Preferences → Terminal. Only applies if the notice is enabled there.
modal_conn.prompt_regex_hint: Regular expression that identifies the prompt line when the shell does not emit OSC 133; the blocks panel uses it to segment the buffer. Empty = default pattern.
modal_conn.environment_hint: Shows an environment badge on the tab, sidebar, dashboard and status bar, so production stands out at a glance.
modal_conn.allow_legacy_hint: Adds aes-cbc, 3des-cbc, dh-sha1, hmac-sha1 and ssh-rsa to the negotiation. Lowers security: only use with old servers.
modal_conn.legacy_select_hint: Choose which legacy algorithms to offer during negotiation:
modal_conn.agent_forwarding_hint: Reuses the local agent socket ($SSH_AUTH_SOCK) to authenticate hops from the remote host.
modal_conn.agent_forwarding_warning: Enable it only on trusted hosts: a compromised server can use your agent (and your keys) to hop to other machines.
modal_conn.agent_forwarding_confirm_message: Agent forwarding shares your local SSH agent with the remote host. If that host is compromised, it could use your keys to hop to other machines. Enable it only on trusted hosts. Do you want to enable it for this profile?
modal_conn.disable_paste_confirm: Don't confirm risky pastes for this profile
modal_conn.disable_paste_confirm_hint: Skips the confirmation preview when pasting multiline, very long or control-character text in this profile's sessions.
modal_conn.x11_forwarding_hint: Requires a local X server at localhost:6000 (DISPLAY=:0). On Windows or macOS you need a dedicated X server.
modal_conn.auto_reconnect_hint: 0 = disabled. Number of automatic reconnect attempts after a drop, with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s…).
modal_conn.persist_session_hint: On connect, a named session on the server is reattached (or created): if the connection drops or you close the app, whatever was running stays alive and the next connection picks up where it left off. Requires tmux or screen on the server; if missing, a normal shell opens and you are warned.
modal_conn.session_log_hint: Dumps the shell output to a log file at session_logs/<profile>-<timestamp>.log inside the data directory.
modal_conn.proxy_jump_hint: Connect to this bastion host first and tunnel an SSH channel to the actual target (ProxyJump). Reuses the profile credentials.

modal_credential.passphrase_message: Enter the passphrase for {target}'s private key. You can leave it empty if it has none.
modal_credential.remember_password: Save password in the system keyring
modal_credential.remember_passphrase: Save passphrase in the system keyring

import_ssh.title: Import ~/.ssh/config
import_ssh.no_hosts: No valid Host entries found in the file

import_wizard.title: Import connections
import_wizard.workspace_hint: Imported connections will be created in a new workspace with this name.
import_wizard.pw_intro: The file contains encrypted passwords. You can optionally import them.
import_wizard.master_hint: Leave blank if you never set a password in mRemoteNG (the default will be tried).
import_wizard.pw_mode_unsupported: Unsupported cipher mode: {mode}. Only GCM is supported.
import_wizard.pw_continue_without: The master password is invalid; passwords will not be imported. Continue with connections only?
import_wizard.err_xml: The file is not valid XML.
import_wizard.err_not_mremoteng: This does not look like an mRemoteNG export.
import_wizard.err_not_asbru: This does not look like an Ásbrú Connection Manager export.
import_wizard.err_yaml: The YAML file is not valid: {detail}
import_wizard.err_full_encryption: This file uses full-file encryption (FullFileEncryption); it cannot be read without decrypting the whole file. Not supported yet.
import_wizard.err_yaml_bomb: The file abuses YAML references (anchors and aliases) and expanding it could exhaust your machine's memory. It won't be imported.
import_wizard.err_too_many: The file declares too many connections (maximum {max}).
import_wizard.err_too_deep: The file's folder tree exceeds {max} nesting levels.
import_wizard.err_no_supported: No connections of a supported protocol (SSH/RDP) found in the file.

modal_hostkey.title: Unknown host
modal_hostkey.intro: This is the first time you connect to {host}:{port} and there is no stored key for this server.
modal_hostkey.advice: Verify it with the server's administrator over a channel you trust. If you accept, it will be stored and you'll be warned if it ever changes.

modal_hostkey_changed.title: The server's key has changed!
modal_hostkey_changed.intro: The identity of {host}:{port} does NOT match the recorded one. This can happen after a server reinstall or key rotation… or if someone is intercepting the connection (man-in-the-middle attack).
modal_hostkey_changed.advice: Accept ONLY if you expected this change and can verify the new fingerprint through a trusted channel. Accepting replaces the old entry and the connection continues; rejecting changes nothing.

key_setup.title: Passwordless access
key_setup.intro: Rustty will set up SSH key access to “{name}” ({host}): it will use your ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 key (created if missing), install it on the server by authenticating with the current password, and check that it works BEFORE changing the profile.
key_setup.config_msg: Also add an alias to your ~/.ssh/config so you can connect with `ssh` from any terminal? Existing entries are never modified.
key_setup.working: Installing the key on the server…
key_setup.done_verified: Key access verified: the profile now connects without a password ({path})
key_setup.done_unverified: The key was installed but verification failed; the profile was not changed
key_setup.failed: Could not set up key access

modal_ftpscert.title: Unknown FTPS certificate
modal_ftpscert.intro: This is the first time you connect over FTPS to {host}:{port} and there is no stored certificate for this server.
modal_ftpscert.advice: Verify it with the server administrator over a trusted channel. If you accept, it will be stored and we’ll warn you if it changes.

modal_paste.title: Confirm paste
modal_paste.reason_multiline: This text contains multiple lines and could run commands in the shell.
modal_paste.reason_control: This text contains control characters that could inject terminal sequences.

prefs_terminal.title: Terminal
prefs_terminal.hint: Behavior of SSH terminals and the local console.
prefs_terminal.copy_on_select_hint: Selected text is copied to the clipboard automatically
prefs_terminal.right_click_paste_hint: Right click on the terminal pastes the clipboard
prefs_terminal.confirm_risky_paste_hint: Ask for confirmation before pasting multiline, very long or control-character text
prefs_terminal.share_command_history_hint: Stores commands typed in any session and offers them from the multiline editor (Ctrl+Shift+E) in every tab. Not synced to the cloud.
prefs_terminal.capture_screen_hint: Saves each (non-private) SSH session output to disk for “Connect and restore previous screen”. May contain sensitive data; not synced.
prefs_terminal.sftp_verify_size_hint: Checks the final size of the copied file to detect incomplete transfers.
prefs_terminal.ligatures_hint: Requires a font with ligature support (FiraCode, JetBrains Mono, Cascadia Code…). Applied to new sessions only.
prefs_terminal.renderer_hint: On GPU the terminal survives massive output without freezing the interface; if acceleration fails or is lost it falls back to CPU and retries the GPU once it recovers. Choose “CPU only” if you see flicker or artefacts (virtual machines, old drivers). Applies to new sessions.
prefs_terminal.cmd_notify: Notify when a long command finishes
prefs_terminal.cmd_notify_hint: Uses the shell's OSC 133 marks (modern bash/zsh/fish). With the session in view it stays quiet; with the app focused it shows a toast; in the background, a system notification. Only duration and exit code: the command's output is never captured.
prefs_terminal.local_cwd_hint: Folder where new local consoles open. Empty = your home folder. If the path doesn't exist, the home folder is used.
prefs_terminal.highlight_hint: Each rule colors the pattern matches in the terminal buffer. Matches that span a network chunk are not highlighted.

prefs_appearance.title: Appearance
prefs_appearance.terminal_theme_hint: If left on "Same as UI", the terminal inherits the theme above.
prefs_appearance.theme_io_hint: The new format uses simple tokens like base, text, blue, or red. Copy the template, change colors, and import it.
prefs_appearance.density_hint: Adjusts spacing and row height across the sidebar, tabs and modals without changing terminal size. “Spacious” increases line spacing for readability.
prefs_appearance.text_size_hint: Raises the minimum chrome text size (menus, lists, bars) without touching the terminal or the UI zoom.
prefs_appearance.bg_hint: Optional local image behind the terminal, with opacity and blur to taste. It never syncs, and with a background active the minimum text contrast rises to AA on its own.
prefs_appearance.bg_set_hint: Background applied. Already open sessions fully adopt it after reconnecting.
prefs_appearance.bg_gif_too_big: The animated image exceeds the 4 MB limit.
prefs_appearance.bg_store_error: Could not store the image (local storage full).
prefs_appearance.color_blind_safe_hint: Differentiates status dots (tabs, sync, status bar) by shape in addition to color.
prefs_appearance.search_all_workspaces_hint: If disabled, the home and sidebar searches only show connections from the active workspace.
prefs_appearance.ui_zoom_hint: Scales the rail, sidebar, tabs and modals without affecting the terminal. Also via Ctrl+Alt and +/−/0.
prefs_appearance.contrast_hint: Strengthens the contrast of text, borders, focus and selection without changing theme. Affects the whole interface.
prefs_appearance.reduce_motion_hint: Disables animations, long transitions and decorative spinners. The operating-system preference is honored too.
prefs_appearance.view_fade_hint: Brief transition between the start panel and the terminal when opening or closing sessions. "Reduce motion" also disables it.
prefs_appearance.strong_focus_hint: Increases the thickness and contrast of the focus ring during keyboard navigation.
prefs_appearance.overlay_scrollbars_hint: The thumb floats over the content, thin at rest and wider on hover. Turn it off for the plain thin scrollbars.
prefs_appearance.native_scrollbars_hint: Restores the wide, always-visible scrollbars of the operating system, with no styling of our own. For anyone who needs a large target or more contrast; it overrides the overlay mode.
prefs_appearance.term_contrast_hint: Adapts hard-to-read ANSI colors in the terminal so text reaches a minimum contrast against its background. Useful with low-contrast themes.
prefs_appearance.term_cursor_highvis_hint: Paints the cursor with a high-contrast ink (black or white depending on the background) in any style and thickens the caret when the style is "bar".

prefs_keepass.title: KeePass
prefs_keepass.hint_html: Use passwords from a .kdbx database instead of the system keyring. The DB is decrypted in memory and locked when the app closes.
prefs_keepass.autolock_hint: The countdown only resets when you actually use the database (looking up or inserting a credential), not with terminal activity.
prefs_keepass.lock_on_suspend_hint: If the machine suspends or hibernates with the database open, it locks on wake.

prefs_data.title: Local data
prefs_data.hint_html: Export your connections to a JSON file for backup or migration. Passwords are not included.

prefs_import_external.title: Import from other applications
prefs_import_external.hint: Migrate your connections from other managers. A step-by-step wizard rebuilds the folder tree and, optionally, decrypts saved passwords (all locally).

prefs_security.title: Security
prefs_security.hint: How Rustty handles sensitive actions. Nothing is blocked here: you choose the behavior.
prefs_security.broadcast_paste: Paste password while broadcast is on
prefs_security.broadcast_paste_hint: What to do when pasting the profile password (Ctrl+P) while broadcast mode is replicating input across multiple panes.
prefs_security.strict_host_key: Confirm the fingerprint on first connection
prefs_security.on_wake: When the machine wakes up or the network returns
prefs_security.on_wake_reconnect: Check and reconnect the dropped ones
prefs_security.on_wake_hint: After a suspend, a session may still look connected even though its connection is already dead. Reconnections are staggered so they don't overwhelm the server.
prefs_security.strict_host_key_hint: The first time you connect to a server, show its key fingerprint and ask for confirmation before storing it. If you turn this off, the first key is accepted and remembered automatically (TOFU): convenient, but a man-in-the-middle present on that first connection would go unnoticed.
prefs_security.host_key_change_prompt: Ask when a server's key changes
prefs_security.host_key_change_prompt_hint: If the key of a known server changes (the classic sign of a man-in-the-middle, but also of a reinstall), show a warning with both fingerprints and let you decide: accepting replaces the old entry and the connection continues; rejecting changes nothing. If you turn this off, the change is always rejected and known_hosts must be edited by hand.
prefs_security.strict_ftps_cert: Confirm the FTPS certificate on first connection
prefs_security.strict_ftps_cert_hint: FTPS servers with a self-signed certificate (a NAS, an internal machine) are accepted by fingerprint just like SSH keys: the first time the certificate fingerprint is shown and confirmation is asked; afterwards, a certificate change is rejected. If you turn this off, the first fingerprint is remembered automatically.
prefs_security.broadcast_ask_message: Broadcast mode is active on {n} panes. Where do you want to paste the password?

prefs_known_hosts.title: Known host keys
prefs_known_hosts.hint: Review the fingerprints stored in ~/.ssh/known_hosts and remove conflicting entries without editing the file by hand.

prefs_session_logs.title: Session logs
prefs_session_logs.hint: Sessions with recording enabled dump the shell output to log files. Set a retention policy so they don't pile up indefinitely.
prefs_session_logs.warning: Logs may contain sensitive information (executed commands and their output). Store and delete them with care.
prefs_session_logs.stats_error: Could not read the logs folder
prefs_session_logs.no_limits_set: Set a maximum age or size before cleaning up
prefs_session_logs.prune_error: Could not clean up the logs: {err}

modal_known_hosts.title: Known host keys
modal_known_hosts.hint: Entries from ~/.ssh/known_hosts. Remove a conflicting key to accept it again the next time you connect.
modal_known_hosts.confirm_remove: Remove this known_hosts entry? You will have to trust the host key again when you reconnect.

prefs_credentials.title: Credentials
prefs_credentials.hint_html: Manage local credentials, KeePass, and reusable variables in one place. Each source keeps its own storage and security lifecycle.
prefs_credentials.local_hint_html: Store reusable passwords or tokens in the system keyring and reference them with ${master:name}. The value is never included in Rustty's catalog.
prefs_credentials.variables_hint_html: Store non-secret text values and reuse them with ${var:name} in profiles, snippets, and commands.
prefs_credentials.warn_shared: Reusing the same credential across several hosts means that, if it is compromised, all of them are affected at once.
prefs_credentials.confirm_delete_msg: Delete this credential? The stored value will be removed from the keyring.
prefs_credentials.referenced_warn: The credential is in use by {n} profile(s). Delete it anyway?

modal_credential_edit.kind_hint_master: The value is stored encrypted in the keyring and never shown.
modal_credential_edit.kind_hint_var: Non-secret text variable: stored in the catalog and can be viewed.
modal_credential_edit.kind_hint_secret: The value is stored encrypted in the keyring and never shown.
modal_credential_edit.name: Name
modal_credential_edit.name_invalid: Invalid name: no spaces; must start with a letter or “_” and contain only letters, digits, “_”, “-” or “.”.

modal_ask.title: Connection details
modal_ask.message: This profile needs some details before connecting.

modal_dup.title: Duplicate session with changes
modal_dup.message: New session of “{name}” ({host}). Changes only apply to this session; the profile is not modified.
modal_dup.passphrase_message: Leave empty if the key has no passphrase.

prefs_aesthetics.title: Aesthetics
prefs_aesthetics.sftp_layout_hint: Choose which side of the file panel shows the remote directory; the local one stays on the opposite side.

prefs_transfer.title: FTP/SFTP
prefs_transfer.hint: File transfer options for SFTP, FTP and FTPS.
prefs_transfer.notify_done_hint: With the session in view it stays quiet; with the app focused it shows a toast; in the background, a system notification. Errors always notify; successes only if the transfer was long or over 10 MiB.
prefs_transfer.sftp_verify_size_hint: Checks the final size of the copied file to detect incomplete transfers.
prefs_transfer.sftp_max_concurrent_hint: Parallel SFTP requests per transfer. Raise it for more speed on high-latency networks; lower it (e.g. 4) if the server returns “Handle limit reached” (Hetzner Storage Box and similar). Applies to new sessions.

resizer.hint: Arrow keys to adjust; Home to reset

status.cwd_seg_nav: Go to {path} in the SFTP panel
status.cwd_nav_error: Could not open the SFTP panel at {path}

metrics.title: Resources
metrics.kill_message: SIGTERM will be sent to “{cmd}” (PID {pid}) on the server. If the process ignores it, it will still show up in the next sample.

prefs_sync.title: Cloud sync
prefs_sync.hint: Sync profiles, preferences, themes and shortcuts across devices. End-to-end encrypted (E2E) with your passphrase. The server only sees opaque data.
prefs_sync.local_cloud_hint: You can point this to a local folder, NAS or system-synced folder.
prefs_sync.icloud_hint: Uses iCloud Drive as a synced local folder. Available on macOS with iCloud Drive enabled.
prefs_sync.snapshots_hint: Pick a previous snapshot and click "Restore" to overwrite your current state with that version.
prefs_sync.snapshots_confirm: This will replace your profiles, preferences, themes and shortcuts with those in the selected snapshot. Continue?
prefs_sync.snapshots_diff_none: The snapshot is identical to the current state: restoring will change nothing.
prefs_sync.auto_interval_hint: Checks for changes from other devices at a regular interval while the app is open. You choose the interval; if nothing changed, nothing is touched.
prefs_sync.history_keep_hint: Number of encrypted snapshots to keep before pruning. Startup checks for changes; sync only writes when local/remote differ.
prefs_sync.webdav_pass_hint: Stored in the OS keyring under service rustty, key sync:webdav_password.
prefs_sync.oauth_missing_app_credentials: This build has no built-in OAuth credentials for Google Drive.
prefs_sync.passphrase_hint: Encrypts data before upload. If you lose it, you lose access to sync. Stored in the OS keyring.
prefs_sync.secrets_hint: When saved passwords are enabled, Rustty reads them from the local keyring, encrypts them with the sync passphrase, and restores them into the keyring on other devices. The unlocked KeePass database is never synced.
prefs_sync.never_synced: The unlocked KeePass database is never synced.
prefs_sync.offline_toast: No connection to the sync server. It will retry automatically.
prefs_sync.bad_passphrase_toast: The local passphrase can't decrypt the remote state (changed on another device?). Update it in Preferences → Backups.
prefs_sync.clock_skew_warn: This computer's clock differs from the server by about {min} min. Sync may resolve conflicts unexpectedly; check the system time.
prefs_sync.rotate_current_msg: Enter the passphrase the remote state is encrypted with.
prefs_sync.rotate_new_msg: The remote state will be re-encrypted with the new passphrase. Other devices will ask to update it.
prefs_sync.rotate_history_q: Also re-encrypt the historical snapshots with the new passphrase? Otherwise they stay encrypted with the old one.
prefs_sync.rotate_bad_old: The current passphrase can't decrypt the remote state.
prefs_sync.on_exit_hint: If unsynced changes remain when closing the app, runs a quick final sync (max 3 s) so they aren't lost until the next start.
prefs_sync.tombstones_hint: Days each deletion is remembered so it can't "resurrect" from another device. Pick "Keep forever" if any device stays off for months.
prefs_sync.device_name_hint: Other devices will show this name in their sync activity instead of the identifier.
prefs_sync.boot_indicator_hint: Shows a discreet notice in the lower corner while the startup sync runs.
prefs_sync.journal_empty: No cycles with changes recorded yet.
prefs_sync.first_sync_message: The server already contains synced data. Applying the first merge will:
prefs_sync.wipe_hint: Deletes the encrypted state and all history from the server, and clears the local cache. Your local data (profiles, themes…) is untouched.
prefs_sync.wipe_confirm_message: The encrypted state and all historical snapshots will be deleted from the server, and the local cache cleared. Your local profiles and preferences are untouched. Continue?

prefs_about.title: About Rustty
prefs_about.hint: Cross-platform terminal client and connection manager.
prefs_about.open_release: A new version ({version}) is available. Open the downloads page?
prefs_about.update_install_prompt: New version {version} available. Download and install now?

prefs_system.title: System
prefs_system.autostart_hint: Adds Rustty to the list of applications that start automatically at login.
prefs_system.rdp_display_hint: Default for RDP sessions; each profile can override it. The resizable window can be maximised and dragged, and the remote desktop follows the size: needs Windows 8 / Server 2012 or newer. «Fixed size» is the previous behaviour, for servers that do not support it.
prefs_system.restore_work_tabs: Offer to restore last session tabs
prefs_system.restore_work_tabs_hint: Saves the tab order and their profiles (never terminal contents, secrets or private sessions) and offers to reconnect them in bulk at startup.
prefs_system.autostart_minimized_hint: When started with the system, hide the window and keep only the tray icon.
prefs_system.metrics_hint: Shows CPU, memory, disk, network and processes of the remote server over the SSH connection itself, with nothing to install. Linux only for now.
prefs_system.metrics_enabled_hint: If off, turn the monitor on by hand with the button in the status bar for each session.
prefs_system.metrics_rate_hint: Each sample is a light read over SSH; a shorter interval updates more often at the cost of a little more traffic.
prefs_system.metrics_alerts: Warn when a threshold is exceeded
prefs_system.metrics_alerts_hint: With the monitor on, shows a warning when the server's CPU, memory or a disk goes above the chosen percentage. Each metric warns once per episode (it does not repeat while it stays high).
